pr_title: Removed optimization causing Dictionary indexing to use named get.
pr_body:
Fixes #44241

Test project with script code can be found in that issue, and this fix can be verified against that example.

This removes what claims to be an optimization, but the optimization uses "named get" instead of "keyed get" or "indexed get" for this purpose. @vnen may want to look at re-adding this optimization correctly in the future.

cc @vnen @reduz
pr_comments: If you want to update this PR with the changes I suggested we can merge it.
I feel this PR is only a half-measure, so I implemented the full fix (as per my comment) here: #48139, which also fix the Lua-style notation using String for keys instead of StringName.

issue_context.title: Dictionary element are not available by index
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
custom d0f1c03b4


**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10

**Issue description:**
Cannot find existing key in Dictionary

**Steps to reproduce:**
Empty project
Create node
Add script 
`func _ready():
	var dict: Dictionary = {
		"elem1": 1,
		"elem2": 2,
	}
	print(dict)
	print(dict["elem1"])`

Output:
{elem1:1, elem2:2}

Debug:
Invalid get index 'elem1' (on base: 'Dictionary').

**Minimal reproduction project:**
[bugreport.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5668913/bugreport.zip)
comments:
I can confirm `dict["elem1"]` or `dict.elem1` don't work in current master. It seems to be related to failed comparison between `String` and `StringName` types.

For info, as a workaround you can use the syntax `dict.get("elem1")` which still works.

hit this when looking up bone names in a dictionary. since I already made it, here is a reproduction project: run dictnames.tscn
[gdscriptbugs.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5754700/gdscriptbugs.zip)

had some trouble with .get() ... I mean, it avoids a crash yes but produces the wrong result. I just worked around by iterating through all keys and checking equality.
looks as if this has hit a brick wall. Dictionary's might need an overhaul similar to what vnen is doing with Arrays.
does anyone know if this is going to be fixed/addressed? I have to think that there are many people that are expecting Dictionaries to work as they did before.

> does anyone know if this is going to be fixed/addressed? I have to think that there are many people that are expecting Dictionaries to work as they did before.

The `master` branch isn't meant to be used for production, so it may take a while for this to be fixed.

review_comments:
I would actually do something like this:

```
if (subscript->index->is_constant && subscript->index->reduced_value.get_type() == Variant::STRING_NAME)
```

So it works properly for every case (using `STRING_NAME` as an index is actually the same as get named).

There's another issue in the analyzer though, which is already doing this by adding a new node to the tree (which is something I tend to avoid but it seems to have slipped):

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0ee744ff5f3cf045a2699aa4111de3200b9d70be/modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp#L2631-L2639

This code could be removed in favor of making the check on the compiler.
